name: Script Color-Code Asset Map
use_when: A scripted video needs many screen recordings, images, videos, overlays, animations, or text beats.
The editor wants to reduce timeline searching by collecting assets before the edit.
A long voiceover script needs sentence-level visual planning.
avoid_when: The edit is unscripted and discovery-based.
The video is a quick trim or talking-head clip that does not need many assets.
The color categories are so vague that they do not change asset decisions.

timeline_pattern.pattern: script -> sentence_tags -> asset_type -> collect_assets -> import_bins -> timeline_layering
timeline_pattern.tag_rule: Assign each sentence or beat a practical visual category before collecting assets.
timeline_pattern.asset_rule: Gather screen recordings, images, video clips, text cards, overlay needs, and animation placeholders based on the tags.
timeline_pattern.bin_rule: Organize collected assets by category and script beat so the timeline pass is fast.

motion.rule: Mark animation placeholders before building them; do not leave complex animation decisions hidden inside the edit pass.

sound.rule: Mark SFX and music needs during script tagging, then place final cues after visual timing is known.

captions.rule: Mark where captions are enough versus where center text or scene-attached text is needed.

color.rule: Use the tag map to keep asset style and color coherent across clips, images, overlays, and animations.

implementation.ffmpeg: Represent the plan as CSV/JSON with beatStart, beatEnd, sentenceSummary, assetType, assetPath, and visualJob fields.
implementation.remotion: Store scriptBeats with colorTag, assetRefs, visualComponent, captionMode, and sfxNeed before rendering.
implementation.blender: Use the map to decide which beats need separate animated inserts before building scenes.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Color-label script lines externally, gather media into folders, then import and place by tag.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use bins and markers for script categories such as screen record, image, video, text, overlay, animation, and SFX.

common_mistakes: Opening the NLE with no asset plan and searching for every visual mid-edit.
Using broad categories that do not tell the editor what to collect.
Collecting assets that are keyword-related but do not serve the script beat.
Forgetting animation placeholders until the timeline feels empty.
qc: Does every scripted sentence or beat have a visual category or a deliberate no-visual decision?
Are required assets collected before the heavy timeline pass?
Do asset bins match the script categories?
Does each placed asset map to a script beat?
Are animation placeholders listed before animation work begins?
